baseline.prior_evidence_policy: Historical partial results are context only. They do not qualify the final release artifacts.

milestones.title: Audit and acceptance inventory
milestones.exit: Every requirement, supported platform, provider build, test entry point, and environmental dependency has an owner and an evidence path.

milestones.title: Shared executable Core contracts
milestones.exit: One immutable Core wheel passes R4 conformance and R3 history tests in both installed consumers; executable contract status is evidence based.

milestones.title: Composition persistence and authority
milestones.exit: HTTP-only MCP, additive migrations, canonical identity, scoped tickets, session capabilities, and operator authorization pass their positive and negative cases.

milestones.title: Inventory consent and reusable bindings
milestones.exit: Local and remote onboarding creates an approved binding through public entry points and reuses it without repeating technical setup.

milestones.title: Canonical operation dispatcher
milestones.exit: All user intents use one durable admission and dispatch path; loss of a response, cancellation, or retry never creates a second native effect.

milestones.title: Embedded execution through the product
milestones.exit: An installed Nexus and Core open, submit, control, observe, and close a local runtime using canonical admission with no Connector application installed.

milestones.title: Remote daemon lanes leases and execution
milestones.exit: The real Connector daemon performs R4 negotiation, paginated reconciliation, correlated attach and lease installation, and remote open and controls from the Nexus dispatcher.

milestones.title: Durable events receipts and replay
milestones.exit: Events and receipts survive restart and reconnect with contiguous post-commit ACKs, bounded journals, explicit gaps, and publisher recovery without a new native event.

milestones.title: Canonical decisions and native input
milestones.exit: An authorized decision produces exactly one native application and a recoverable receipt while preserving full request identity, namespace, and sensitive input rules.

milestones.title: Direct tools and governed work
milestones.exit: Direct MCP HTTP and the qualified Pi native bridge reach the same authorized domain with exclusive consumption, causal results, and no Connector MCP proxy.

milestones.title: Complete UI CLI and US English
milestones.exit: Human and headless user journeys pass through the actual UI and CLI; all application-authored visible and returned text is US English.

milestones.title: Recovery revocation shutdown and limits
milestones.exit: Process crashes, partitions, rotation, disk pressure, and shutdown preserve ownership and uncertainty without unbounded queues or unauthorized effects.

milestones.title: Migration cutover and removal of duplicate execution
milestones.exit: Legacy data and active ownership migrate with restartable checkpoints and verified rollback; obsolete execution paths are removed after demonstrated parity.

milestones.title: Final artifacts and complete acceptance
milestones.exit: The immutable three-repository release tuple passes all applicable TR4, TN, J, language, platform, provider, and installed-product campaigns with no unresolved required test.

additional_requirements.requirement: All application-authored UI, accessibility, CLI, API, MCP, WebSocket, error, diagnostic, and return messages use US English, including legacy surfaces.

acceptance_policy.test_assignment: Each original scenario is assigned to the latest closing milestone of its source task IDs and is reassessed on final artifacts in M13.
acceptance_policy.not_applicable_requires: A normative capability or platform exclusion, its negative test, and an explicit recorded rationale; missing infrastructure is NOT_RUN, never NOT_APPLICABLE.
acceptance_policy.commit_policy: Commit coherent tested increments and push feature/v0.2.0 in each changed repository; milestone closure requires all acceptance evidence, independently of commit count.
